title: Is RingCentral’s AI Receptionist worth it?
summary: Dive into RingCentral’s AI Receptionist features. Learn what it does, what it costs, and how it compares to alternatives like Quo.
body_markdown:
[RingCentral](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-alternatives) is one of the oldest business phone platforms on the market. It mixes legacy features like desk phones with newer technology like cloud-based phone systems. This includes the RingCentral AI Receptionist, also known as AIR.


RingCentral’s AI receptionist supports call handoffs, appointment booking, and SMS follow-ups. These are all appealing features for small and growing businesses. But they come with several drawbacks you should know.


In this article, we cover RingCentral AI Receptionist’s pricing, features, and limitations. Not a fan of what you find? We’ll also share a strong alternative.


##


**What is the RingCentral AI Receptionist?**


RingCentral’s AI Receptionist is an AI-powered tool that talks to customers in real time without human employees. It understands and speaks to customers in natural human language. Plus, it can handle multiple inbound calls at once.


##


**What can the RingCentral AI Receptionist do?**


RingCentral’s AI Receptionist comes with features like:


- [Intelligent call routing](https://www.quo.com/blog/intelligent-call-routing/) **.** When callers use specific verbal keywords, RingCentral’s AI can route callers to the right departments or people. No need to rely on a human receptionist or legacy IVR for basic call forwarding.
- **Multiple language support.** Thanks to natural language processing, AIR can detect and respond to multiple languages. It currently supports English, Spanish, French, Japanese, German, and more.
- **PBX integration.** The standalone version of RingCentral’s AI receptionist can integrate with SIP-based PBX systems. This is useful if you still have traditional phone equipment and want to modernize it with the AIR.


- **Book appointments.** AIR can act as an[AI appointment setter](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/appointment-setter) by scheduling meetings and generating meeting links. It also integrates with Google Calendar and Outlook. That way, callers can book appointments without talking to an agent.
- **Answer FAQs.** RingCentral’s AI receptionist can pull information from a knowledge base to answer common questions. For example, if a customer asks, “What time do you close?” the AIR can inform the caller.
- **Custom greetings.** You can customize the message and tone of your AI receptionists’ greeting. You can also set different messages for both office hours and after hours.
- **Automated text messaging.** Send customers SMS follow-up messages like booking confirmations, feedback forms, or links. Let agentic AI handle routine tasks, and save time for more complex customer messages.
- **Customizable persona.** Control the voice, language, and tone of your AI receptionist. For example, if you’re a law office and speak in a more professional tone, you can update RingCentral’s AI receptionist to reflect that.


##


**How much does the RingCentral AI Receptionist cost?**


You can get RingCentral’s AIR in three ways: by itself, as an add-on, or in a bundle.


As mentioned, the standalone version lets you use AIR outside of the RingCentral platform with another business phone system. The AIR + RingEX bundle lets you pay a single RingEX subscription to access both tools at once. There’s also a third option: add the AI Receptionist to an existing[RingCentral plan](https://www.quo.com/blog/ringcentral-pricing) . You’ll pay your plan’s base rate, plus the add-on.


Here’s a breakdown of the prices you can expect for each:


AI Receptionist Standalone AIR + RingEx Bundle AI Receptionist Add-on


$49 per month $39 per month for AIR + $15 per month for one user on the RingEX Core Plan $39 per month added to existing RingEX subscription


All AI Receptionist plans include 100 free minutes of use, with a $0.50 per minute pay-as-you-go charge for going over. Keep in mind all calls are rounded up to the next minute, even if you’re only three seconds past the mark.


##


**RingCentral AI Receptionist limitations to keep in mind**


The RingCentral AI Receptionist is a high-tech option for picking up customer calls. But it *does* have some downsides that make it a poor option for small businesses.


Let’s take a closer look:


### **Costs pile up quickly**


The AI Receptionist includes 100 free minutes per month, which seems like a lot at first glance. But it might disappear quickly if your business fields a lot of calls.


Let’s say your business takes five calls a day, with five minutes spent talking to the AI Receptionist. That’s 25 minutes of your AI Receptionist’s time per day. Multiply that by five days a week and four weeks per month, and you’ll have used the AI Receptionist for at least 500 minutes. That’s 400 minutes over your 100-minute limit. And at $0.50 per minute, you’ll spend an extra $200 in one month.

What happens if you get an unexpected wave of incoming calls? Or when your call volume spikes during the busy season? Be prepared for your AI Receptionist usage costs to spike.


The good news is RingCentral’s isn’t the only option. Quo’s[Sona AI](https://www.quo.com/sona) receptionist, for example, charges per call and not per minute. This is much more manageable for small businesses and makes monthly costs easier to estimate.


### **No flexibility around call routing**


You can use the AIR receptionist to share[business hours](https://www.quo.com/product/call-routing/business-hours-call-routing?ps_partner_key=OTFjZjEyZWM4ODEw&ps_xid=Cv1VlSMETp1Qk8) and company greetings. It also sends follow-up texts and books appointments via Google and Outlook calendars.


But you *can’t* customize when it will or won’t answer. By default, the AI automatically answers *all* incoming calls — which may include occasional spam. There’s no intelligent routing solution that makes the AI receptionist a last-resort option. If your team is busy, you can’t make your receptionist a fallback option. You also can’t manually select the AI receptionist as a menu option.


To summarize: you can’t save money by using the AIR selectively. If you switch it on, it’s on for everything — potentially costing hundreds in unnecessary minutes per year.


### **The AI Receptionist knowledge base comes with limitations**


Your AI agent is only as effective as the knowledge base that feeds it. If an agent can’t access enough relevant information, it can’t answer customer questions intelligently.


One RingCentral user on[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/ringcentral-ai-receptionist-air/reviews/ringcentral-ai-receptionist-air-review-13330731) found that the AI Receptionist imposes a 500-character limit on knowledge base articles. That’s about 71 to 125 words — not much information when describing a complex product or service.


### **Struggles with off-script requests**


Some G2 reviewers say the AI Receptionist struggles with edge cases and multi-part questions. This can confuse callers and create stress when they’re looking for basic information.


One reviewer wrote:


*“There is still room for improvement when dealing with unusual or very derailed customer requests, where a live representative is often needed. I also think additional customization options for responses and workflows would make it even more flexible for businesses with unique requirements.”* —[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/ringcentral-ai-receptionist-air/reviews/ringcentral-ai-receptionist-air-review-13375596)


### **Inconsistent data retrieval**


RingCentral customers say that AIR can struggle to pull information from the knowledge base. It may also ignore reference documents or struggle to fetch complex answers.


This can lead to problems like:


- **Callers getting frustrated.** *“Sometimes customers would reach me already frustrated because they had spent time with the AI and still couldn’t get their issue resolved.”* —[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/ringcentral-ai-receptionist-air/reviews/ringcentral-ai-receptionist-air-review-13364447)
- **Incorrect answers.** *“Hallucinations and edge cases: struggles with complex or off-script questions, occasionally giving wrong answers instead of gracefully transferring.” —*[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/ringcentral-ai-receptionist-air/reviews/ringcentral-ai-receptionist-air-review-13394954) **


##


**5 Other key limitations to RingCentral**


RingCentral’s AI Receptionist is meant to be used within the RingCentral ecosystem. So it’s only fair you’re aware of some of the platform’s limitations.


This includes:


- **SMS/MMS limits.** The base plan only allows 25 messages per user per month. You’ll need to upgrade to add more messages. Keep in mind there’s no “unlimited” tier available.
- **Limited toll-free calling.** RingCentral’s base plan only includes 100 toll-free minutes per month. If you need more, you’ll have to upgrade.
- **Call storage limits.** There’s a universal 90-day limit on call recording storage. That means you’ll lose access to previously recorded conversations unless you download each file, even if you’re on the “unlimited” storage tier.
- **Shared SMS inbox is locked.** The shared inbox feature isn’t available on the base plan. You either need to upgrade or purchase an add-on for $25 extra per month.
- **No native auto-reply feature.** You can’t automatically reply to missed calls, texts, or voicemails in RingCentral. Instead, you need to install an app from their app marketplace. This requires extra time and effort for your team.


##


**A better alternative to RingCentral**


RingCentral’s AI receptionist can help you *get started* with AI voice agents. But it’s not necessarily where growing teams *stay* . More than 90,000 businesses have chosen a more modern business phone solution: Quo. It brings calling, texting, and customer information together into one AI-powered platform.


Quo’s AI receptionist, Sona, can be easily customized to handle calls when your team is unavailable. It offers many of the same features you get with AIR, including[setting appointments](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/appointment-setter) , lead capture, and[IVR](https://www.quo.com/product/ai/ivr) . Plus, Quo offers features you can’t get with RingCentral — all with per-call pricing for Quo’s AI receptionist, not per minute.

### **Control when Sona handles calls**


Quo includes a drag-and-drop call flow builder that lets you control when inbound callers meet your AI receptionist. You can decide which calls Sona takes and when, such as after business hours. You can place Sona in whatever order makes sense for your company.


For example, you might set Sona to only take calls if nobody else answers. Worried about spam calls? Set up conditional routing. That way, callers not saved in your contacts go to Sona first, and not a busy member of your team.


### **Business-friendly pricing**


Quo’s base plan includes 10 free Sona calls per month. You can upgrade to a paid plan if you need more. Additional calls cost $1 per call on the free tier, but we disable overages by default to prevent unexpected charges.


Quo’s Sona lets you choose from multiple pricing tiers to easily scale based on your team’s needs. Unlike RingCentral, we bill per call rather than per minute. Pricing starts at $25 per month for 40 calls. Calls under 15 seconds don’t count toward your usage.

### **Setup is quick and simple**


Setting up Sona is an easy, three-step process. Just pick the number you want Sona to use in your Settings panel, and follow the Setup Wizard’s instructions:

2. Define what Sona should say or do on the call.

Once you’ve set up Sona, you can customize it further by choosing where it fits in your call flow. Add instructions for Sona on how to handle different scenarios, like which calls or questions it automatically routes to your reps. You can always run a test call with Sona and add more information to its knowledge base if needed.


### **Easily add the information you need to train Sona**


As mentioned, RingCentral’s AI Receptionist only allows for 500-character knowledge base articles. These don’t offer much depth for product or company information. Quo, on the other hand, allows up to 20,000 characters per page.


Quo’s setup wizard explains what you need to do to build a comprehensive knowledge base for your product and your company. For example, if a customer asks about a return policy, you can point Sona directly to the right page. Sona can then give the customer complete, accurate information.


You can also build a vocabulary of custom keywords that Sona recognizes as unique to your business. This makes it easier for Sona to pull the right information from your database. For example, you might add “emergency dispatch” as a keyword so Sona knows to immediately transfer to an on-call rep. Or you might train Sona to recognize the phrase “quarterly treatment.” That way, it can automatically pull up the right service description and text that caller a booking link during the call.


### **Integrate with 9,000+ apps**


Quo offers thousands of connections to different third-party apps. You can automatically log calls handled by your team and Sona, send SMS messages after the customer completes a form, and more.

### **Capture leads over text**


Whenever a new customer texts your business, Sona for lead capture can text them back right away. It can ask them what product or service they’re interested in. Or it can gather general information your team needs to qualify leads or follow up later.


Each Sona call results in a conversation transcript and summary. This will appear in an internal conversation thread with the relevant customer details, so you can spot key information at a glance. It also tags members of your team so they can take over. If you need to delegate more tasks, just tag them yourself in another internal thread.

##


**FAQs**


****Do I need a RingCentral phone system to use RingCentral AI Receptionist?****


No, you don’t need a dedicated RingCentral business phone system to use its AIR tool. A standalone option integrates with SIP-based PBX networks. That way, you can connect it to your existing, legacy phone system.


****What features does RingCentral’s AI Receptionist offer?****


RingCentral’s AI agent offers appointment booking, SMS follow-ups, and IVR. It also supports multiple languages, including Spanish, French, and Japanese.


****Are there any hidden costs with RingCentral’s AI receptionist?****


RingCentral includes 100 minutes on every plan. After that, you’ll pay an extra $0.50 per additional minute. Keep in mind RingCentral rounds up to the nearest minute, whether your call is 1:52 or 1:01 minutes long.


****Does the RingCentral AI Receptionist offer a free plan?****


There’s a 14-day free trial for RingCentral’s AI receptionist. But there’s no free plan available on any tier. Your best option is to test the platform for 14 days, then cancel your subscription before the two-week period is up.
